analysis.title: Robust US jobs market boosts December rate hike chances
key_insights: October US non-farm payrolls rose 165k versus a 75k consensus forecast, with 84k of upward revisions to the prior two months.
The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Wage growth was 0.4% MoM / 3.1% YoY versus consensus of 0.3% / 2.9%.

ING says the report supports a December Fed rate hike. Expectations for the hike had slipped to close to 50:50 at one point in recent days. About 20bp is now priced for the December FOMC meeting, and ING fully expects the Fed to deliver.
Private education and healthcare services led job gains (+53k). Manufacturing added 19k and has added 86k jobs over the past five months after three consecutive years of decline.
ING attributes the manufacturing recovery to secure and relatively low-priced energy, a strong economy, large tech investment spending and, at the margin, tariffs.
Other sectors: temporary help +19k, transport and warehousing +25k, leisure and hospitality -13k, construction -3k.

ING expects a December hike followed by a long pause and doubts the need for additional hikes next year. The market no longer fully prices additional hikes in 2027, which ING links to the big drop in energy prices and diminished fears of second-round price effects.
Next week's CPI report is expected to show core CPI up 0.2% month-on-month, which ING says should support the pause story.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds pricing for December FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Pricing is back to a full 20bp hike after slipping to close to 50:50. ING expects the Fed to deliver.
A 0.2% core print would support the view that the Fed hikes in December and then pauses.

risk_factors: A hot core CPI print next week would challenge the view that the Fed hikes in December and then pauses.
Energy prices fell sharply, and ING's no-further-hikes view relies on that holding along with diminished second-round price effect fears.
